answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence decays with distance. A sybil cluster can gain voting weight only through connections to trusted nodes; if these form a sparse external cut, low conductance limits random-walk flow across the boundary. Given bounded degrees and a limited seed mass inside the cluster, this constrains its aggregate vote: like nectar reaching an orchard across a narrow jetty, internal links cannot create independent trust.
